_citation: ISO 286-2:2010, Shigley's Mechanical Engineering Design (10th ed.), Machinery's Handbook (31st ed.)
_note: Maps functional keywords to recommended ISO 286 fit classes with rationale. Append-friendly for future expansions (feeds/speeds data sits beside this).

fits.rationale: Large clearance for freely rotating parts in poor alignment or temperature variation. Not intended for precision bearing surfaces.
fits.notes: H11/d11 is the go-to when fit doesn't matter much; H9/d9 for moderate precision needs.

fits.rationale: Moderate clearance for rotating parts that need lubrication. Good general-purpose running fit.
fits.notes: H8/f7 is widely used for precision running fits. Requires lubrication.

fits.rationale: Small controlled clearance for sliding without rotation. Parts can be assembled/disassembled by hand.
fits.notes: Classic precision sliding fit. 20H7/g6 gives 0.007-0.041mm clearance on 20mm nominal.

fits.rationale: Very small clearance for precision fits; parts can be pushed together by hand under light pressure.
fits.notes: Smallest reliable clearance class. H7/h6 gives near-zero to small clearance.

fits.rationale: Precise location with minimum clearance. Allows assembly/disassembly without press.
fits.notes: Tightest reliable clearance. H7/h6 is the most common precision-location class.

fits.rationale: Transition fit: slight clearance or slight interference depending on actual sizes. Location without relying on press fit.
fits.notes: k6 gives primarily clearance with occasional zero-play; n6 gives slight interference. Both require a key or pin to transmit torque.

fits.rationale: Light interference fit requiring a press. Provides good location and limited torque transfer without keys on smaller diameters.
fits.notes: 50H7/p6 gives 0.001-0.042mm interference — press fit, not hand assembly. Verify with fit_calc.

fits.rationale: Substantial interference requiring hydraulic press or thermal expansion. Reliable torque and axial load without fasteners.
fits.notes: r6 is moderate press; s6 is heavy press. Thermal assembly recommended for large diameters.

fits.rationale: Dowel pins need interference or tight transition to maintain location under repeated assembly.
fits.notes: Use p6 for permanent dowels, n6 for removable. Material matters: steel in aluminum vs steel in steel.

fits.rationale: Rolling bearing inner ring on shaft: k6 for rotating inner ring with light load, m6/n6 for heavier loads.
fits.notes: Follow bearing manufacturer recommendation. ISO 286 fits may be tighter than generic table when outer ring rotates.

fits.rationale: Rolling bearing outer ring in housing: typically clearance or transition for stationary outer ring, to allow creep if misloaded.
fits.notes: Clearance fit is standard unless bearing supports rotating load — then use interference on outer ring.
